items.prompt: To add EF Core persistence, the guide says to keep IWorkforceReadModel stable and swap the adapter in DI. What does that buy?
items.answer: Only the adapter and its DI line change; controllers stay as they are
distractors: EF attributes can then go directly on the Domain entities
The in-memory seed data is migrated into the database automatically
The dashboard no longer needs its application-level tests
items.explanation: The application port is listed as a strong choice: it allows persistence migration without changing controllers.

items.prompt: Today InMemoryWorkforceReadModel is registered with AddSingleton. What lifetime should the EF adapter's DbContext have, and why?
items.answer: Scoped: a DbContext is per-request state that must not be shared
distractors: Singleton, to keep the caching behavior of the in-memory model
Transient, so that each query opens its own database connection
Singleton, because migrations need one long-lived context instance
items.explanation: The migration guidance explicitly says to add a scoped DbContext, not a singleton adapter.

items.prompt: To keep rollback possible when moving to a database, which change does the guide deploy first?
distractors: The application code that uses the new tables
The data migration or backfill
Removal of the in-memory adapter
items.explanation: Order: schema, then code, then data changes - old code keeps running on the new schema, and the in-memory adapter stays selectable by config.

items.prompt: Worker.RequiresAttention inspects ComplianceChecks. What failure mode does the guide predict once workers come from EF?
items.answer: N+1 queries, if compliance checks load lazily for each worker on the dashboard
distractors: A null reference, because EF never populates navigation collections
Wrong results, because high-risk checks get filtered out in SQL
A deadlock between the worker table and the compliance table
items.explanation: Calling a navigation-dependent property per worker can trigger one query per worker; also note the dashboard reads all workers unbounded.

items.prompt: When does a worker require attention?
items.answer: Status NeedsAttention, or an unresolved high-risk compliance check
distractors: Only when the worker's status is set to NeedsAttention
Any high-risk compliance check, whether resolved or not
Whenever onboarding progress is still below 100 percent
items.explanation: The rule is a domain invariant kept near the data - one of the critique's strong choices.

items.prompt: What does Money.Add do when the two values have different currencies?
distractors: Converts at the current exchange rate
Returns the first value unchanged
Adds and keeps the first currency code
items.explanation: The value object guards its own invariant (currency comparison is case-insensitive) and returns a new value via `with`.

items.prompt: A hiring quote asks for an employer-of-record hire in a country where EOR is unavailable. Where is it rejected, and how does the caller see it?
items.answer: The calculator returns a failed Result; the controller maps it to ProblemDetails
distractors: The HTML form blocks it with a min attribute before any request is sent
Model binding rejects it because of a data annotation on HiringQuoteRequest
The domain throws an exception, which the pipeline turns into a 500 response
items.explanation: Validation lives in the application service; HiringQuoteRequest has no attributes, so shape validation is minimal.

items.prompt: The QuoteBuilder form uses an HTML min on compensation. Why is that not enough?
items.answer: Clients can call the API directly and skip the form
distractors: Browsers ignore min on number inputs entirely
The min attribute only applies after submission
React strips HTML validation attributes at build
items.explanation: Seniors distinguish input-shape validation, business validation and authorization; the calculator rejects non-positive compensation.

items.prompt: WorkforceController has [ApiController] and [Route] but no [Authorize], and Program registers no auth services. How does the guide classify this?
items.answer: A possible risk, not a confirmed bug, unless the API is exposed
distractors: A confirmed bug that leaks payroll data in production today
Safe, because CORS restricts which browsers may call the API
Safe, because the current endpoints accept no worker IDs at all
items.explanation: The guide is careful with confidence: the repo is a demo; the risk becomes real only on exposure.

items.prompt: When the dashboard API call fails, workforceApi.ts catches the error and returns mockDashboard. Why is that rated a high risk?
items.answer: A real outage looks like working data to users
distractors: The mock data contains real worker names and salaries
The catch block retries forever and freezes the UI
It makes the API itself return 500 for every request
items.explanation: Fix: gate the fallback by environment and show explicit error states; add the UI error state before disabling the fallback.

items.prompt: The UI's mock fallback computes quotes itself. What risk does the critique name?
items.answer: Quote math duplicated in the UI fallback can drift
distractors: TypeScript rounding produces negative fees
Mock quotes ignore the employment type
The UI posts the fallback quote to the server
items.explanation: Suggested move: remove the fallback quote math or generate mocks from a fixture.

items.prompt: Owning this EOR app for three months, what does the critique do first?
items.answer: Auth, tenant scoping and API tests
distractors: Replacing the in-memory model with EF
Generating TypeScript types from DTOs
Structured logs around the quote flows
items.explanation: Order: security, contract reliability, persistence, observability, frontend resilience.

items.front: How does the critique plan to roll out auth and persistence safely (migration / tests / rollback)?
items.back: Auth: add middleware and policies, then protect endpoints; 401/403 API tests; feature-flag enforcement in non-prod first. Persistence: EF adapter behind the existing port; existing app tests plus DB integration tests; keep the in-memory adapter selectable by config.

items.front: Authorization drill for GET /api/workforce/dashboard: which two pieces of the DTO need separate decisions?
items.back: Who can view payroll totals (DashboardDtos.cs:13-19) and who can view worker names (DashboardDtos.cs:21-32) - aggregate financials and personal data are different permissions.

items.front: Why does seeding with DateTime.UtcNow make tests unstable, and the fix?
items.back: Seeded dates shift every run, so date-dependent results change with the wall clock. Inject time (a clock/TimeProvider) so tests can pin it.
